_doc: Historical oil-supply disruptions used as analogs. Every figure is real and cited (prov R). The on-screen 'similarity' is a COMPUTED metric (see src/lib/analogs.ts), never a measured or invented percentage — it weighs chokepoint overlap, disrupted volume, and price move against the current scenario.

analogs.name: Iran–Iraq Tanker War
analogs.resolution: Ended with the Iran–Iraq War ceasefire (UN Res. 598, Aug 1988); US Navy reflagged/escorted Kuwaiti tankers (Operation Earnest Will).
analogs.note: Persistent attacks on Gulf/Hormuz shipping (451 attacks, ~239 tankers hit) but at peak disrupted <2% of Gulf traffic; oil flow was not significantly cut and prices fell through the 1980s.

analogs.name: Abqaiq–Khurais attack
analogs.resolution: Aramco drew on inventories and other fields; output restored in ~2 weeks and prices fell back below pre-attack levels.
analogs.note: Drone/missile strike knocked out 5.7 mb/d (~5% of world supply). Brent spot 61.25 → 68.42 (+11.7%), the largest single-day gain in a decade.

analogs.name: Ever Given / Suez blockage
analogs.resolution: Refloated on the 6th day (Mar 29 2021) by 14 tugs plus dredging and a spring tide; traffic backlog cleared within ~2 weeks.
analogs.note: A single grounding shut the Suez Canal for 6 days (~$9bn/day of goods; ~3–5 mb/d of seaborne oil delayed). Brent spot low 59.96 → 63.77 (+6.4%).

analogs.name: Red Sea / Houthi crisis
analogs.resolution: Not fully resolved in period; mitigated by rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope (+10–16 days) and naval escorts (Operation Prosperity Guardian).
analogs.note: Bab el-Mandeb oil transit fell from 8.7 mb/d (2023) to 4.0 mb/d (2024). Diversions round the Cape add ~10–16 days; Brent trough 74.21 → 84.57 (+14%). The closest analog to a two-strait scenario.
